questions.questionText: In cyclic voltammetry (CV) of an electrochemically reversible redox couple in solution, $O + ne^- \rightleftharpoons R$ (where both oxidized and reduced species are freely soluble in the electrolyte), the potential of a stationary planar working electrode is scanned linearly back and forth at scan rate $\nu$. Which of the following diagnostic criteria correctly identify an ideal reversible diffusion-controlled electrochemical process at $298\text{ K}$?
options: A) The peak-to-peak potential separation between the anodic and cathodic current peaks satisfies $\Delta E_p = |E_{pa} - E_{pc}| \approx \frac{59\text{ mV}}{n}$, and is theoretically independent of scan rate $\nu$.
B) The peak current $i_p$ is directly proportional to the square root of the scan rate ($i_p \propto \nu^{1/2}$), as described by the Randles-Sevcik equation.
C) For a kinetically sluggish (irreversible) electron transfer process, the peak separation $\Delta E_p$ progressively decreases as the scan rate $\nu$ is increased.
D) For a chemically stable and reversible couple, the ratio of anodic peak current to cathodic peak current is equal to unity ($|i_{pa} / i_{pc}| = 1.0$).
questions.explanation: Step 1: For a Nernstian reversible couple where interfacial charge transfer is rapid compared to semi-infinite linear diffusion, the peak potentials are given by $E_{pa} = E_{1/2} + \frac{1.109 RT}{nF}$ and $E_{pc} = E_{1/2} - \frac{1.109 RT}{nF}$. Step 2: The peak potential separation at $298\text{ K}$ is $\Delta E_p = E_{pa} - E_{pc} = \frac{2.218 RT}{nF} = \frac{0.059\text{ V}}{n} = \frac{59\text{ mV}}{n}$, which is invariant with scan rate, confirming statement A. Step 3: The Randles-Sevcik relationship for a reversible couple states: $i_p = (2.69 \times 10^5) n^{3/2} A D^{1/2} C \nu^{1/2}$. Peak current scales directly with $\nu^{1/2}$, characteristic of planar semi-infinite diffusion, confirming statement B. Step 4: When the electrogenerated product is chemically stable on the voltammetric timescale, all species reduced during the forward scan are available for re-oxidation on the reverse scan, yielding $|i_{pa} / i_{pc}| = 1.0$, confirming statement D. Statement C is incorrect because for quasi-reversible or irreversible systems, finite charge transfer kinetics cause peak separation $\Delta E_p$ to increase as scan rate increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: For the Daniell cell reaction: $\text{Zn}(s) + \text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) \to \text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Cu}(s)$ operating reversibly at $298\text{ K}$, the standard cell EMF is $E^\circ = 1.100\text{ V}$ and its temperature coefficient at constant pressure is $\left(\frac{\partial E^\circ}{\partial T}\right)_P = -1.00 \times 10^{-4}\text{ V K}^{-1}$. When $1.0\text{ mol}$ of zinc reacts reversibly in this galvanic cell, determine the reversible heat exchanged with the surroundings ($q_{\text{rev}} = T\Delta S^\circ$). (Take $1\text{ F} = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$).
questions.explanation: Step 1: The standard reaction entropy change $\Delta S^\circ$ of a galvanic cell reaction is related to the temperature coefficient of cell potential by $\Delta S^\circ = nF\left(\frac{\partial E^\circ}{\partial T}\right)_P$. Step 2: In the Daniell cell, $n = 2$ moles of electrons are transferred per mole of zinc reacted. Substituting values gives: $\Delta S^\circ = 2 \times 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1} \times (-1.00 \times 10^{-4}\text{ V K}^{-1}) = -19.30\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$. Step 3: For a reversible electrochemical process at constant temperature, the reversible heat exchanged with the surrounding thermostat is $q_{\text{rev}} = T\Delta S^\circ$. Step 4: Substituting $T = 298\text{ K}$ yields: $q_{\text{rev}} = 298\text{ K} \times (-19.30\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}) = -5751.4\text{ J mol}^{-1} = -5.75\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. The negative sign indicates that this quantity of heat is dissipated to the surroundings during reversible galvanic discharge. Distractor $+5.75\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ has an inverted sign, while $-218.05\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ represents total reaction enthalpy $\Delta H^\circ$, and $+212.30\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ represents maximum electrical work $-\Delta G^\circ$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In the modern membrane chlor-alkali industry, brine (concentrated aqueous $\text{NaCl}$) is electrolyzed in a membrane cell employing a perfluorosulfonate cation-exchange membrane (such as Nafion). Which of the following statements correctly describe the electrochemistry, transport mechanisms, and selectivity of this industrial process?
options: A) The perfluorosulfonate membrane allows free migration of both sodium cations and hydroxide anions across the compartments to equalize pH.

B) The cation-exchange membrane selectively allows $\text{Na}^+$ ions to migrate from the anode compartment to the cathode compartment, while rejecting $\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{OH}^-$ anions due to electrostatic Donnan exclusion by fixed $-\text{SO}_3^-$ groups.

C) At the cathode, water is reduced to hydrogen gas and hydroxide ions ($2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 2e^- \to \text{H}_2 + 2\text{OH}^-$) because $E^\circ(\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{H}_2, \text{OH}^-) = -0.83\text{ V}$ is far more positive than $E^\circ(\text{Na}^+/\text{Na}) = -2.71\text{ V}$.

D) At the anode, $\text{Cl}^-$ is oxidized to $\text{Cl}_2$ in preference to $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ oxidation, even though $E^\circ(\text{O}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}) = +1.23\text{ V} < E^\circ(\text{Cl}_2/\text{Cl}^-) = +1.36\text{ V}$, primarily because the overpotential for oxygen evolution is substantially larger than that for chlorine evolution on dimensionally stable anodes (DSA).
questions.explanation: Step 1: In the chlor-alkali membrane cell, saturated brine enters the anode chamber and water enters the cathode chamber. At the cathode, reduction of water ($2\text{H}_2\text{O} + 2e^- \to \text{H}_2 + 2\text{OH}^-$, $E^\circ = -0.83\text{ V}$) occurs much more favorably than reduction of sodium ($E^\circ = -2.71\text{ V}$), generating $\text{H}_2$ gas and $\text{OH}^-$, confirming statement C. Step 2: The cation-exchange membrane contains covalently bound negatively charged sulfonate groups ($-\text{SO}_3^-$). These fixed negative charges electrostatically repel co-ions ($\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{OH}^-$) via Donnan exclusion, while permitting counter-ions ($\text{Na}^+$) to migrate toward the cathode. This prevents hydroxide ions from entering the anode compartment where they would react with chlorine, confirming statement B and refuting statement A. Step 3: Thermodynamically, water oxidation to oxygen ($E^\circ = +1.23\text{ V}$) has a lower potential than chloride oxidation to chlorine ($E^\circ = +1.36\text{ V}$). However, on DSA electrodes ($\text{RuO}_2/\text{TiO}_2$), the kinetic overpotential for $\text{O}_2$ evolution is very high ($>0.5\text{ V}$), whereas that for $\text{Cl}_2$ evolution is very low ($<0.05\text{ V}$). Hence, chlorine discharge dominates, confirming statement D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In acidic aqueous solution, the dark-green manganate(VI) ion ($\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$) is unstable and undergoes spontaneous electrochemical disproportionation into purple permanganate ($\text{MnO}_4^-$) and solid manganese dioxide ($\text{MnO}_2$) according to the stoichiometric redox equation: $3\text{MnO}_4^{2-}(aq) + 4\text{H}^+(aq) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{MnO}_4^-(aq) + \text{MnO}_2(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$. Given standard electrode reduction potentials at $298\text{ K}$: $E^\circ(\text{MnO}_4^-/\text{MnO}_4^{2-}) = +0.56\text{ V}$ and $E^\circ(\text{MnO}_4^{2-}/\text{MnO}_2) = +2.26\text{ V}$. Determine the number of moles of electrons ($n$) transferred in this balanced chemical equation as written.
questions.explanation: Step 1: Separate the disproportionation reaction into two distinct half-reactions. In the oxidation half-reaction, manganese is oxidized from oxidation state $+6$ in $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$ to $+7$ in $\text{MnO}_4^-$: $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}(aq) \to \text{MnO}_4^-(aq) + e^-$. Step 2: In the reduction half-reaction, manganese is reduced from oxidation state $+6$ in $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$ to $+4$ in $\text{MnO}_2$: $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}(aq) + 4\text{H}^+(aq) + 2e^- \to \text{MnO}_2(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$. Step 3: To balance the electron transfer between the two half-reactions, multiply the oxidation half-reaction by 2: $2\text{MnO}_4^{2-} \to 2\text{MnO}_4^- + 2e^-$. Summing the multiplied oxidation half-reaction and reduction half-reaction yields: $3\text{MnO}_4^{2-}(aq) + 4\text{H}^+(aq) \to 2\text{MnO}_4^-(aq) + \text{MnO}_2(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$. Step 4: The total number of electrons cancelled and transferred in the balanced cell reaction as written is $n = 2$. Substituting into the answer yields 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText: In modern lithium-ion secondary cells, energy storage occurs through reversible intercalation/deintercalation of lithium ions within host interstitial lattices. A standard cell utilizes a graphite intercalation anode ($\text{Li}_x\text{C}_6$) and a lithium cobalt oxide cathode ($\text{Li}_{1-x}\text{CoO}_2$) immersed in a non-aqueous electrolyte of $\text{LiPF}_6$ dissolved in organic alkyl carbonates. Which of the following electrochemical statements regarding this system is/are correct?
options: A) During charging of the battery, $\text{Li}^+$ ions deintercalate from the transition metal oxide cathode and migrate through the electrolyte to intercalate into the graphitic carbon anode.
B) Pure liquid water can serve as an ideal non-volatile solvent in commercial high-voltage ($4.2\text{ V}$) lithium-ion cells due to its exceptionally high dielectric permittivity.

C) The solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) passivation layer formed on the graphite anode during initial charge cycles must be electronically insulating to halt further solvent decomposition, while remaining ionically conducting to allow $\text{Li}^+$ passage.
D) During cell discharge, lithium metal plates out as metallic dendrites on the surface of the positive electrode.
questions.explanation: Step 1: During the charging process, an external power supply drives electrons into the negative graphite electrode while extracting electrons from the positive $\text{LiCoO}_2$ electrode. To maintain electroneutrality, $\text{Li}^+$ ions deintercalate from $\text{Li}_{1-x}\text{CoO}_2$ and migrate through the separator to intercalate between graphene sheets: $\text{Li}_{1-x}\text{CoO}_2 + x\text{Li}^+ + xe^- \to \text{LiCoO}_2$ in reverse, confirming statement A. Step 2: The operating cell voltage of a Li-ion battery ($3.7 - 4.2\text{ V}$) vastly exceeds the thermodynamic electrochemical stability window of liquid water ($1.23\text{ V}$). In aqueous media, water would rapidly undergo electrolysis into $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$, and metallic/intercalated lithium would react violently, refuting statement B. Step 3: Graphite operates at a potential near $0.1 - 0.2\text{ V}$ vs $\text{Li}/\text{Li}^+$, well below the reductive stability limit of organic carbonate solvents ($\approx 0.8\text{ V}$). During the initial formation cycles, controlled solvent reduction generates an insoluble passivation film (SEI) comprising $\text{Li}_2\text{CO}_3$, lithium alkyl carbonates, and $\text{LiF}$. This SEI layer must be electronically insulating to stop electron tunneling and parasitic electrolyte reduction, yet ionically porous to facilitate $\text{Li}^+$ transport, confirming statement C. Step 4: Statement D is incorrect because during discharge, lithium ions intercalate into the cathode host lattice without any metallic lithium plating.
